records.issue_text: Uniqueness is enforced only by the client-side refine: the server schema (addGuests.schema.ts:6) and the handler's `uniqueGuests` filter never dedupe within a single request, so a direct API call with `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` either inserts duplicate attendee rows or trips the `(bookingId, email)` constraint.
records.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: addGuests.schema.ts defines guests as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness refine, and the handler's `uniqueGuests` filter only excludes emails already among `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails — it does not dedupe within the request. So `guests: ["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` passes validation and createMany would insert duplicate attendee rows (or fail on any unique constraint). The client-side refine in AddGuestsDialog is easily bypassed via direct API call.
